data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 names a 'refuted if' condition but the substantive relation it actually states is incomplete: it abstracts the error-correction trajectory into 'Cognitive Scaffolding Efficiency' and asserts reliability gains are refuted if performance drops when the checklist is removed, yet it never identifies what the abstraction stands in a dependence, reduction, or integration relation WITH — it mentions SRC_003's trajectory as the thing being abstracted, but the refutation condition ('performance drops significantly when the checklist is removed') tests a dependency claim (tool-dependence vs. expertise-integration) without naming the target of the dependence or what is integrated into what. The artifact says the gain 'was a dependency on the tool rather than an integration of expertise into the non-experts,' which gestures at a contrast but does not state a substantive relation kind (dependence, integration) between 0bb6167c36cf and a neighbourhood member — it only summarizes the two endpoints (external memory structure vs. internalized expertise) and adds a falsification condition. A refuted-if clause attached to a bare contrast is not itself the named relation the problem requires.
